request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now have an approver, and that user can approve or reject the person's PENDING claims the way a steward can. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 approver tests.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V109__person_approver.sql`, adds a nullable `approver` column to `person`.

**Server:**
- `Person` holds the approver, and `PersonView` sends it to the screen.
- `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/people/{id}/approver` sets the approver. Leaving the name blank clears it. It writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=… by=… name=<person> user=<user>` to the audit file.
- In `ClaimService`, the check behind approve and reject now lets in a steward or the person's approver. The existing rule still stands: whoever opened or last edited a claim can't approve it.

**Front end** (`people.ts`): each person's row has a new Approver column (`person-approver`), plus a text box (`person-approver-input`) and a "Set approver" button (`person-approver-save`). If the save is refused, the row's error shows.

Decisions for you:
- **Anyone signed in can set an approver.** The request didn't say only a steward may, so I didn't restrict it, unlike flagging. If only stewards should be able to set one, that's a small change; say if you want it.
- **The approver stays on the sheet it was set on.** Cloning a sheet or transferring a person doesn't carry it over.
